item.title: “Good sirs, if a monk, reflecting, knows: ‘I dwell much with a greedy mind; I dwell much with a hateful mind; I dwell much with…
item.description:
“Good sirs, if a monk, reflecting, knows: ‘I dwell much with a greedy mind; I dwell much with a hateful mind; I dwell much with a mind overcome by sloth and torpor; I dwell much with restlessness; I dwell much with doubt; I dwell much with anger; I dwell much with a defiled mind; I dwell much with bodily fever; I dwell much with laziness; I dwell much with an unconcentrated mind’ — then that monk should make a strong wish, arouse effort, be energetic, strive, be strong-minded, not fall away, be mindful and clearly comprehending for the abandonment of those evil, unwholesome states. Just as, good sirs, if a turban or head were on fire, one would make a strong wish, arouse effort, be energetic, strive, be strong-minded, not fall away, be mindful and clearly comprehending to extinguish that turban or head — so too, that monk should make a strong wish … for the abandonment of those evil, unwholesome states. If a monk, reflecting, knows: ‘I dwell much with a mind free from greed; I dwell much with a mind free from hatred; I dwell much with a mind free from sloth and torpor; I dwell much with a mind free from restlessness; I dwell much with a mind that has overcome doubt; I dwell much with a mind free from anger; I dwell much with an undefiled mind; I dwell much with a body free from fever; I dwell much with an energetic, striving mind; I dwell much with a concentrated mind’ — then that monk, established in those wholesome states, should further devote himself to the destruction of the defilements.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.52

item.title: “Through many a birth in samsara I have wandered, Seeking but not finding the builder of this house. Suffering is birth again and again.” “O…
item.description:
“Through many a birth in samsara I have wandered,
Seeking but not finding the builder of this house.
Suffering is birth again and again.”

“O house-builder, you are seen!
You shall not build a house again.
All your rafters are broken,
Your ridge-pole is shattered.
My mind has attained the unconditioned,
And the extinction of craving has been reached.”

From: Dhammapada 146-156

item.title: “‘For life, the arahants have abandoned unchastity, live the holy life, live secluded, abstaining from sexual intercourse, the low practice. Today, this night and day,…
item.description:
“‘For life, the arahants have abandoned unchastity, live the holy life, live secluded, abstaining from sexual intercourse, the low practice. Today, this night and day, I too abandon unchastity, live the holy life, live secluded, abstaining from sexual intercourse, the low practice. In this factor, I follow the arahants and will observe the uposatha day.’”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 8.41

item.title: - What hangs up the world? What envelops the world? What closes in the world? Upon what does the world stand? - Craving hangs up…
item.description:
- What hangs up the world?
What envelops the world?
What closes in the world?
Upon what does the world stand?
- Craving hangs up the world,
Aging envelops the world,
Death closes in the world,
Upon suffering the world stands.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.67

item.title: “Here, venerable sir, a person has no stain but does not truly know: ‘There is no stain in me.’ For such a person, it can…
item.description:
“Here, venerable sir, a person has no stain but does not truly know: ‘There is no stain in me.’ For such a person, it can be expected: ‘He will attend to the sign of the beautiful. By attending to the sign of the beautiful, greed will pollute his mind. He will die with greed, with ill-will, with delusion, with stain, his mind polluted.’ Venerable sir, just as a bronze bowl brought from the market or from the smithy, clean and pure, and the owner does not use it, does not wipe it, and throws it into a dusty place – that bowl, after a time, becomes more defiled and dustier.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 5 – Anaṅgaṇasutta

item.title: “Monks, how is a monk one who does not know forms? Here, monks, a monk does not know as it actually is all form, namely…
item.description:
“Monks, how is a monk one who does not know forms? Here, monks, a monk does not know as it actually is all form, namely the four great elements and form derived from the four great elements. Thus, monks, a monk does not know forms. Monks, how is a monk one who is not skillful in characteristics? Here, monks, a monk does not know as it actually is the fool and the characteristics of a fool, the wise person and the characteristics of a wise person. Thus, monks, a monk is not skillful in characteristics. Monks, how is a monk one who does not remove the eggs of the gadfly? Here, monks, a monk indulges in arisen sensual thoughts; he does not abandon, dispel, end, or destroy them. He indulges in arisen ill-will thoughts … harmful thoughts … evil, unwholesome states that have arisen; he does not abandon, dispel, end, or destroy them. Thus, monks, is a monk who does not remove the eggs of the gadfly.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 33 – Mahāgopālakasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Vāseṭṭha, there are five factors that cause the growth of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye — desirable, beautiful, delightful, enticing, connected…
item.description:
“Vāseṭṭha, there are five factors that cause the growth of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye — desirable, beautiful, delightful, enticing, connected with sensual pleasure and enjoyment; sounds cognizable by the ear … odors cognizable by the nose … tastes cognizable by the tongue … touches cognizable by the body — desirable, beautiful, delightful, enticing, connected with sensual pleasure and enjoyment. Vāseṭṭha, those five factors that cause the growth of sensual pleasure — the brahmins proficient in the three Vedas, attached, infatuated, bound, not seeing their danger, not understanding the escape from them, enjoy them. Vāseṭṭha, that those brahmins proficient in the three Vedas, abandoning the qualities that make a brahmin, following qualities that do not make a brahmin, attached, infatuated, bound, not seeing their danger, not understanding the escape from them, enjoying them, bound by the bondage of sensual pleasures, could after death be reborn in union with Brahmā — such a thing is not possible.”

From: Dīgha Nikāya 13 – Tevijjasutta

item.title: “What are the five mental shackles not yet cut off? Monks, here a monk is not free from lust, desire, affection, thirst, fever, craving for…
item.description:
“What are the five mental shackles not yet cut off? Monks, here a monk is not free from lust, desire, affection, thirst, fever, craving for sensual pleasures. Monks, for a monk who is not free from lust … craving for sensual pleasures, his mind does not incline to exertion, commitment, persistence, striving. If one’s mind does not incline to exertion, commitment, persistence, striving, this is the first mental shackle not yet cut off.”

From: Majjhima Nikāya 16 – Cetokhilasutta

item.title: Venerable Todeyya: “One in whom desires do not dwell, One in whom craving is not found, One who has crossed beyond doubt — What is…
item.description:
Venerable Todeyya:
“One in whom desires do not dwell,
One in whom craving is not found,
One who has crossed beyond doubt —
What is the liberation of such a one?”

The Blessed One replied to Todeyya:
“One in whom desires do not dwell,
One in whom craving is not found,
One who has crossed beyond doubt —
There is no other kind of liberation.”

Venerable Todeyya:
“Does such a one have longing,
Or is he free from longing?
Does he have wisdom,
Or is he still acquiring wisdom?
O all-seeing sage, explain this to me,
So that I may know what a sage is, O Sakyan.”

The Blessed One:
“He is free from longing,
Without any longing —
He is wise, not acquiring wisdom.
Thus, Todeyya, know the sage:
Possessing nothing,
Not attached to sensual existence.”

From: Sutta Nipāta 5.10
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Elder Uttarapāla: I am truly virtuous, Reflecting on good purpose. I have abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure, Which are the world’s confusion. Born…
item.description:
Elder Uttarapāla:

I am truly virtuous,
Reflecting on good purpose.
I have abandoned the five strands of sensual pleasure,
Which are the world’s confusion.

Born in Māra’s realm,
Struck by strong darts,
Yet I have escaped
Māra’s snare.

All sensual desires are destroyed,
All forms of existence are demolished.
The path of birth and death is ended —
Now there is no further becoming.

From: Theragāthā 3.12
